what: Centene is the largest managed care company in the United States focused on government programmes. It runs Medicaid plans for states, health insurance exchange plans under the Affordable Care Act, and Medicare plans.
customers: State Medicaid agencies, individuals buying subsidised exchange plans, and Medicare members.
money: managed care contracts with state governments
individual plans sold on the health insurance marketplaces
Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans
moat: Contracts with state Medicaid agencies that take years to win and are rarely moved, plus scale in a market most commercial insurers avoid.
risks: It reported an operating loss in the latest period as exchange medical costs ran far above expectations
States have been removing members from Medicaid rolls after the pandemic
Exchange subsidies expiring would shrink its largest growth market
Net margin is thin even in good years
opportunities: Cash of about $24 billion against $16 billion of debt
Repricing exchange premiums for the next plan year should restore margins if costs are correctly estimated
watch: The health benefits ratio, especially on exchange plans, and Medicaid rate adjustments from states.
